hints: Focus on what giant structure really means, which Period 3 elements are giant and which is a simple molecule?
Remember that phosphorus exists as discrete $P_4$ molecules, so it cannot have a giant structure and can be ruled out straight away.
Consider how the chlorides hydrolyse, $AlCl_3$ and $SiCl_4$ give strongly acidic solutions while $MgCl_2$ gives an almost neutral solution.
walkthrough:
**Use giant structure to filter the elements**

Think of structure first, it is the quickest filter. In Period 3, magnesium and aluminium have giant metallic lattices and silicon has a giant covalent lattice.

Phosphorus is different: $P_4$ is a simple molecular structure with weak van der Waals forces, so it is not giant.

**Use the pH of the chloride with water**

A pH less than 5 means the chloride hydrolyses to make acid. This happens for aluminium chloride and silicon tetrachloride.

Chemical behaviour with water:
$$AlCl_3 + 6H_2O \rightarrow [Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+} + 3Cl^- \text{ then } [Al(H_2O)_6]^{3+} \text{ releases } H^+$$
$$SiCl_4 + 2H_2O \rightarrow SiO_2 + 4HCl$$

**Check magnesium chloride for contrast**

Magnesium chloride just dissolves to give hydrated ions with very little hydrolysis.
$$MgCl_2(aq) \rightarrow Mg^{2+}(aq) + 2Cl^-(aq) \text{, pH about 6 to 7}$$
So magnesium fails the pH less than 5 test, while both aluminium and silicon pass both tests.

options.A: Aluminium fits both conditions, but magnesium does not. Magnesium is giant metallic, yet $MgCl_2$ gives a nearly neutral solution, not pH less than 5.
options.B: Both fit. Aluminium has a giant metallic structure and $AlCl_3$ hydrolyses to give an acidic solution of pH about 3. Silicon has a giant covalent structure and $SiCl_4$ hydrolyses completely to give $HCl$, pH about 2.
options.C: Both fail one test. Phosphorus is simple molecular ($P_4$), not giant, so it is out immediately. Magnesium is giant but its chloride is not acidic enough.
options.D: Silicon fits both tests, but phosphorus does not. Although $PCl_5$ hydrolyses to give acid, phosphorus itself does not have a giant structure, so this pair cannot both be Z.
